# ChessDiary

> ChessDiary is a chess game diary app (Android + Web) that lets players photograph paper
> scoresheets, import games from Chess.com and Lichess, store everything in one library, and
> analyse games for blunders and mistakes using the Stockfish engine.

ChessDiary helps chess players consolidate scattered game records — handwritten tournament
scoresheets, Chess.com games, and Lichess games — into a single library, then surfaces the
tactical patterns behind their losses using Stockfish engine analysis.

## Guides

- [How to Read (and Keep) a Chess Scoresheet](https://chessdiary.app/guides/how-to-read-a-chess-scoresheet): Algebraic notation basics and scoresheet handwriting practices.
- [The Most Common Blunder Patterns in Club-Level Chess](https://chessdiary.app/guides/common-chess-blunders): The tactical motifs responsible for most losses below master level.
- [Opening Principles Every Improving Player Should Know](https://chessdiary.app/guides/chess-opening-principles): Five opening principles that keep improving players out of trouble.
- [How to Photograph a Scoresheet for Accurate OCR](https://chessdiary.app/guides/photographing-a-scoresheet-for-ocr): Lighting, angle, and framing tips for accurate scoresheet parsing.
- [How ChessDiary Reads Messy Handwriting (and When It Can't)](https://chessdiary.app/guides/scoresheet-ocr-messy-handwriting): How Gemini-powered OCR handles unclear handwriting and parse confidence.
- [PGN Import vs. Chess.com/Lichess Sync: Which to Use](https://chessdiary.app/guides/pgn-import-vs-chess-com-lichess-sync): The difference between single-game PGN import and account sync.
- [How to Read a Stockfish Blunder Report](https://chessdiary.app/guides/how-to-read-a-stockfish-analysis-report): What quality labels, centipawn loss, and motifs mean in an analysis report.
- [What Happens When the Analysis Engine Is Unreachable](https://chessdiary.app/guides/what-happens-when-stockfish-is-unreachable): The automatic Stockfish-to-Gemini fallback, explained.
- [The Back-Rank Mate: How It Happens and How to Stop It](https://chessdiary.app/guides/back-rank-mate-how-to-stop-it): Why castled kings get mated on the back rank, three ways to prevent it, and how to spot the combinations that exploit it, with verified board diagrams.
- [Knight Forks: How to Spot Them Before They Happen](https://chessdiary.app/guides/knight-forks-how-to-spot-them): Why knights fork so well, the royal and family fork patterns, and a scan that stops them in your own games.
- [Pins, Skewers and Discovered Attacks](https://chessdiary.app/guides/pins-skewers-and-discovered-attacks): Three line-based tactics side by side: how each works on the board, how to win material with it and how to avoid it.
- [Checkmate Patterns Every Player Should Know](https://chessdiary.app/guides/checkmate-patterns-every-player-should-know): Smothered mate, the Arabian mate, the ladder mate and Scholar's mate, with the key idea and defence for each.
- [King and Pawn Endgames: The Rule of the Square, Key Squares and Opposition](https://chessdiary.app/guides/king-and-pawn-endgames-opposition-key-squares): The three ideas that decide almost every king-and-pawn ending, with engine-checked diagrams.
- [Pawn Structure Basics: Isolated, Doubled and Passed Pawns](https://chessdiary.app/guides/pawn-structure-basics): What each pawn structure means, which weakness and compensation it carries, and which plan it points to.
- [Centipawns and Win Probability: What an Engine Score Really Means](https://chessdiary.app/guides/centipawns-and-win-probability): What an engine score measures, how it maps to winning chances, and how to read swings when reviewing your games.
- [How to Review a Tournament Loss: A Step-by-Step Method](https://chessdiary.app/guides/how-to-review-a-tournament-loss): A 30-minute method for turning a lost game into one concrete rule, and a monthly count that shows your real weakness.
- [Time Management in Classical Chess: Where to Spend Your Clock](https://chessdiary.app/guides/chess-time-management-classical-games): Why players run short of time, how to budget the clock, how to play when time is short, and the scoresheet rule.
- [What to Record in a Chess Journal (and What to Skip)](https://chessdiary.app/guides/what-to-record-in-a-chess-journal): A five-field minimum for a chess journal, the fuller set if you want more, an example entry and a monthly review.
- [Candidate Moves and Calculation: How to Think Before You Move](https://chessdiary.app/guides/candidate-moves-and-calculation): A repeatable routine for choosing a move, shown on two positions from Morphy's Opera Game.
- [The Immortal Game, annotated](https://chessdiary.app/sample-analysis/immortal-game): Anderssen vs. Kieseritzky, 1851, with Stockfish evaluations and the moves where the engine disagrees with the legend.
- [The Evergreen Game, annotated](https://chessdiary.app/sample-analysis/evergreen-game): Anderssen vs. Dufresne, 1852, with Stockfish evaluations.
